label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Dear friends, neighbours, Little Acorns families, and everyone this letter finds its way to,

First, I’m safe. Marmalade is safe too, and I’m staying with my sister in Rondebosch. I know some of you have only heard bits and pieces about the fire, so I wanted to put everything in one place. Please feel free to forward this to anyone who’s been asking.

My phone hasn’t stopped since Saturday night. I’m so grateful for every message, but I’m tired in a way I don’t quite know how to explain, and I can’t answer everyone individually right now. If you’ve written and haven’t heard back, please don’t take it personally. I’ve been crying at just about every kind message, even when I haven’t had the energy to reply.

**What happened**

At around 11:40pm on Saturday, 7 November, a fire started in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road in Observatory. My flat is on the second floor.

Everyone in our block of 14 flats got out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and have since been sent home. That is the most important part of this whole letter.

Our neighbour, Uncle Faizel, banged on every door on our floor in his vest and slippers. That’s how I woke up. I grabbed my phone and Marmalade and got out with nothing else. Marmalade then hid under a car for two hours, which was a horrible extra bit of that night, but she is safe now.

I keep thinking about Uncle Faizel going from door to door. I’m so grateful he did.

The fire department has said it was probably an electrical fault, but they’re still investigating. I don’t know anything more than that, and I don’t want to guess or pass on things that haven’t been confirmed.

My flat has extensive smoke and water damage, and the lounge ceiling came down. The landlord says nobody can move back in for at least six weeks. I’m still working out what can be saved, but for now I’ve lost the use of my home and most of what was in it.

That’s the short version. I’m not ready to tell the whole story over and over, so thank you for understanding if I don’t say much more about the night itself.

**What would actually help**

I hate asking for help. I feel awkward even writing this part, and I felt very strange about a fundraiser being set up for me. Zinhle’s response was, more or less, “Shut up and accept it.” So I’m trying.

The biggest practical thing I need is help with a deposit for a new place. Having somewhere of my own again is what I’m trying to work towards.

There are also a few specific things that would make getting back to work easier:

- Shoes for school, size 6.
- Work clothes, size 34.
- A working laptop, if anyone has an older one they no longer use. It doesn’t need to be fancy. Mine had all my lesson planning on it, and having something to work on would help enormously.

Please don’t feel you need to go out and buy any of these things. If you already have something suitable that you’re happy to pass on, that would be lovely. And if you can’t help financially or practically, please don’t feel you have to apologise.

**What I don’t need right now**

People have been incredibly generous with clothes. I have enough general clothing now—more than enough, actually—and I’ll pass the extras on to other people in the block who need them. Apart from the specific work clothes and shoes above, please don’t send more for me.

I also don’t need food at the moment. My sister’s freezer is full, and I’m being very well fed.

One of my children’s mums left a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday without even knocking. That quiet kindness meant so much. Please know that saying I have enough now isn’t me being ungrateful. You’ve made sure I’m covered, and I’d rather any further help went where it’s needed.

**The fundraiser—and an important warning**

My friend Zinhle has set up a BackaBuddy fundraiser for me here:

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is **R25 000**, and as of this morning it had reached **R11 400**. I’m honestly overwhelmed by that. Thank you to everyone who has donated or shared it.

Unfortunately, there is also a page calling itself **“Thandi Fire Relief”**, as well as a WhatsApp message asking people to EFT money to a Capitec account.

**That is not my fundraiser. The Capitec EFT request is not from me or authorised by me. Please don’t send money to it or forward it as a way to help me.**

I’ve reported it. The BackaBuddy link above is the fundraiser Zinhle set up for me. If someone sends you a different page or banking details claiming to be collecting for me, please don’t assume they’re genuine.

If you’ve already shared the other appeal in good faith, please send a correction to the same people. I know everyone is trying to help, and I’m sorry there’s this extra complication.

**For my Little Acorns families**

To the parents at Little Acorns Pre-Primary: the concert on **27 November is still happening**. Please don’t worry. The Ladybirds will have their crowns.

The 22 crowns I’d taken home to laminate, along with the children’s handprint banner, were lost. That has made me cry too. Those little hands and all their hard work mattered to me. But we’ll work out the concert things.

I’m coming back to school on Wednesday. Please don’t make a big thing of it in front of the children. I’m looking forward to seeing my Ladybirds and having some familiar routine, and I’d really appreciate being allowed to get on with that quietly.

Lastly, thank you. To our neighbours, the people who helped us get out, everyone who has checked in, and everyone helping me through the practical bits: I don’t have a proper answer for all this kindness yet.

I’m sad about my home and my things. I’m also very aware that furniture can be replaced and Marmalade can’t.

I’ll reply to comments and messages slowly as I’m able. Please don’t be offended if I don’t answer your DM, and please don’t feel you need to send another message to check that I saw the first one. There’s a lot coming in, and I’m taking things a little at a time.

Thank you for caring about me. And thank you for passing this on so I don’t have to keep finding the words.

With love,  
Thandi
